title: Let It Be
credit: Simple MidiMan arrangement of the Beatles song — a first real piece, not a transcription of the record
_notation: Per hand, one string per bar. Tokens: pitch (G4, Bb3, C#5), chord [G4 Bb4 D5], rest r. Suffix :n = length in eighths (default 1; fractions like 2/3 allowed). Prefix ~ = tied from the previous token of the same pitch (no new attack). Prefix / = rolled chord. Every bar must sum to 8 eighths.

sections.name: Intro
sections.hint: The whole song is four chords: C, G, A minor, F. Right hand holds each triad twice; left hand sits on the root. Straight time — no swing, no rolls.
sections.coach: Four chords — C, G, A minor, F. That's the whole song.

sections.name: Verse
sections.hint: The tune everyone knows. Right hand is a single line of quarters and halves; left hand stays on the same four roots.
sections.coach: The verse — When I find myself in times of trouble.

sections.name: Chorus
sections.hint: Let it be, let it be. Same easy left-hand roots; the melody sits on E, D and C.
sections.coach: Let it be — the line people sing along to.
